archetype.name: Pocket Passer (aggressive intermediate)
archetype.definition: A tall, second-year rhythm thrower who wins between the numbers at 10-19 yards and leans on one top receiver, but has not yet made the short game, third down or ball security work.

report.headline: Red-zone touchdowns are hiding a below-average, sliding passer.
report.take:
Tyler Shough's box score and his efficiency are telling two different stories. He is fourth in passing touchdowns and 11th in PPR per game, yet 28th in EPA per dropback (-0.022), 33rd in yards per attempt (6.14) and 30th in CPOE. He has the volume, at 39 attempts a game behind a 27th-ranked defense that keeps the Saints chasing, and he has a strong red-zone record. He does not yet have play-to-play efficiency. Through six starts he is a slightly below-average NFL passer who scores a lot.

The good part is real and specific. When he throws 10+ air yards he is producing at a strong level: 0.307 EPA on those attempts and 0.404 on intermediate throws, with positive CPOE there. He is also more willing to throw into tight windows than he was as a rookie, with aggressiveness up from 12.8% to 17.87%. The sack avoidance is a genuine step forward. His pressure-to-sack rate was 48th of 62 last year and has improved to 26.5%, 17th of 37, so he is getting the ball out or away instead of taking the loss. The drag comes from the other end of the field. Throws behind the line have cost 10.7 EPA, third down has cost 20.2 EPA with a 35.8% conversion rate, and shotgun snaps (-0.081 EPA) grade far worse than his small under-center sample (0.185).

The numbers hide two things. First, the touchdowns rest on a red zone that won't hold: 10 TDs on 29 attempts with a +14.5 CPOE is a hot streak, not a skill baseline. Second, the receiving corps is thin. Chris Olave carries the passing game at 0.642 EPA per target, while Bryce Lance (-0.676 on 21 targets) and Alvin Kamara as a receiver are actively costing him. Add three lost fumbles (42nd of 45) and the turnover picture is worse than his 2.1% interception rate suggests.

The direction is the worry. Over the last three games he is at -0.111 EPA per dropback, 5.11 yards per attempt and a -8.4 CPOE. Week 5 against the league's top defense explains part of that. Week 6 against a 23rd-ranked unit (16/30, 144 yards, -17.2 CPOE) explains less, and three touchdowns rescued that box score. His rookie year had better accuracy (7.29 YPA, +1.6 CPOE), so the talent for more is there. Right now, though, he is trending toward the passer his efficiency says he is, not the one his touchdown count suggests.

strengths.title: Wins in the intermediate window
strengths.body: His best football is on throws 10-19 yards downfield, where he is producing near-elite EPA with a positive CPOE, and his overall 10+ air-yard work is strong. It fits a passer who has become more willing to throw tight windows than he was as a rookie. It should largely hold because it is tied to Olave and to a real change in his approach, though two of his interceptions came at that depth.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance has genuinely improved
strengths.body: Last year pressure turned into sacks at a bottom-tier rate. This year he ranks in the top half, and his sack rate sits below the league average. He has taken only three sacks in the last three games, so the gain looks like a real development in a second-year player rather than noise.

strengths.title: Scrambles and short-yardage scoring
strengths.body: He scrambles rarely, but when he does it pays: 0.613 EPA per scramble, with half of them moving the chains. His designed runs gain almost nothing per carry yet have produced two touchdowns, which helps his fantasy floor. The scramble value is sustainable, but the rushing scores on that little efficiency are not something to bank on.

concerns.title: Touchdowns outrunning the efficiency
concerns.body: Ten of his 12 passing touchdowns came in the red zone, where his completion rate is running 14.5 points over expected. That rate is far above anything else in his profile and will not hold. Meanwhile his overall EPA and YPA rank in the bottom third. Expect the touchdown rate to slide back toward his efficiency rather than the reverse.

concerns.title: Third downs and the screen game
concerns.body: His third-down passing has cost more EPA than any other split, facing an average of 8.1 yards to go with a sub-36% conversion rate. Throws behind the line have lost value too, despite an 83% completion rate. Part of this is design and supporting cast, since the screen game and the Lance and Kamara targets are bleeding EPA. But the long-yardage problem is his to solve.

concerns.title: Accuracy slipping, fumbles piling up
concerns.body: His CPOE has fallen three points from his rookie year and cratered over the last three games. His three lost fumbles rank near the bottom of the league. Fumble luck tends to even out, but the accuracy slide spans two different opponents, so it is more than a one-game blip.

trend.note: He opened with 410 yards against Detroit and a +14.1 CPOE gem at Baltimore, then faded. The last three games sit at -0.111 EPA per dropback, a Minnesota no-show and a 144-yard Week 6 saved only by touchdowns.

nextGame.headline: A top-six pass defense that smothers the short game.
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh's defense ranks sixth in EPA and fifth against the pass. It is fifth against short throws, and that is where Shough already struggles. It also gives up the third-fewest QB touchdowns per game and the fourth-fewest QB fantasy points. The opening is downfield: the Steelers rank 27th in explosive pass rate allowed and are middle of the pack on deep throws. That suits the 10+ air-yard game where Shough actually produces. Their offense ranks only 26th in pass EPA but passes heavily (third in pass rate over expected). With their top receivers on IR, Pittsburgh may struggle to build a lead that forces New Orleans into a long-yardage passing script. The Book makes the Saints 3.5-point underdogs with a modest 44.5 total.

Availability leans the Saints' way at the margins. Jordyn Tyson is on IR but traveled with the team, and his listed return date is this game. Any snaps he takes would come out of Bryce Lance's role, which has been a black hole. Right guard Cesar Ruiz, a 90%-snap starter, is questionable with a knee injury but also traveled; losing him would weaken interior protection against a defense with a league-average-plus sack rate. On Pittsburgh's side, safety DeShon Elliott is on IR with a knee injury and a return date of this game. If he is out, the middle of the field should be softer for Shough's intermediate throws. The game is indoors.

keyMatchups.title: Olave against a stingy WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Olave is the engine of this passing game at 0.642 EPA per target. Pittsburgh has held opposing top receivers to roughly break-even EPA per target, third-best in the league. If Olave is muted, Shough has little reliable volume elsewhere, so this matchup largely decides his day.

keyMatchups.title: Juwan Johnson in the soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Tight ends have been the leak in Pittsburgh's coverage, at 0.38 EPA per target (24th). Johnson has been a modestly positive target for Shough. Middle-of-the-field work to the tight end is the most obvious way to stay on schedule against a defense that shuts down short perimeter throws.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into strength
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh ranks fifth against short passes, while Shough is barely positive under 10 air yards and negative behind the line. If Kellen Moore leans on screens and checkdowns, expect a repeat of the third-and-long problem. The explosive-pass weakness argues for staying aggressive.

nextGame.watch: Whether his CPOE recovers from the last-three-game slump, particularly on early downs that keep him out of third-and-8.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should stay: he is the unchallenged starter on a team whose defense will keep forcing him to throw, so 200-plus yards most weeks is a reasonable floor. What will not stay is the touchdown rate. A +14.5 red-zone CPOE and a top-five TD count sitting on bottom-third efficiency point to roughly 1.2-1.8 passing scores a game, not two. The sack avoidance and the intermediate throwing look like real second-year growth. The third-down and accuracy problems are the swing.

The upside case is a healthier receiver room. Tyson replacing Lance's targets would add a viable second option behind Olave, and a move toward more under-center and play-action work would play to his best splits. The downside case is the recent slide continuing, in which case he becomes a 175-200-yard passer whose fantasy value depends on goal-line luck. Expect something in between, around 14-18 PPR points a game, with more volatility than his season average implies.

confidence.note: Six starts, with the red-zone TD streak and the slump against a top defense both resting on small samples.
